steps.body: Grade-3 taught you the first few rungs: ten ones make a ten; ten tens make a hundred; ten hundreds make a thousand. That ladder **keeps climbing.** Ten thousands make a ten-thousand; ten ten-thousands make a hundred-thousand; ten hundred-thousands make one **million**. Every rung is the same rule: ×10.

widget.prompt: Put these place-value names in order, smallest to largest.

misorderFeedback.feedback: A hundred is bigger than a ten (100 > 10) — tens comes before hundreds on the ladder.

widget.missFeedback: Each rung is 10 times the one before it: ones, then tens, then hundreds, then thousands.
widget.successFeedback: Ones, tens, hundreds, thousands — each one 10 times the last.

predict.prompt: Stepping one place to the LEFT multiplies a digit's value by…?
predict.reveal: Each rung of the place-value ladder is a ×10 climb — ones to tens to hundreds. That single ratio builds the whole system.

explanationVariants: A thousand is 10 hundreds — that's the ladder rule: each place is 10 times the one before it.
10 hundreds bundle into 1 thousand, the same way 10 tens bundle into 1 hundred.

widget.prompt: How many hundreds are in one thousand?

commonErrors.feedback: 100 counts how many ONES are in a hundred, a different rung. One thousand is 10 hundreds.
1 would mean a thousand and a hundred are the same size — they're not. A thousand is 10 hundreds.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Every rung up the ladder is exactly 10 of the rung below it.

steps.body: Past a thousand, the ladder keeps its same rhythm with new names: **ten-thousand, hundred-thousand, million.** 10 thousands make a ten-thousand. 10 ten-thousands make a hundred-thousand. 10 hundred-thousands make a million. Same rule, six rungs up from ones.

explanationVariants: 10 times 1 hundred-thousand is 1 million — the top rung on this ladder.
Bundling 10 hundred-thousands together makes exactly 1 million.

options.label: 1 million
options.feedback: 10 hundred-thousands bundle into 1 million — the ladder's next rung.

options.label: 1 ten-thousand
options.feedback: A ten-thousand is SMALLER than a hundred-thousand, not 10 times bigger. 10 × hundred-thousand = 1 million.

options.label: 10 thousand
options.feedback: That skips two rungs. 10 hundred-thousands make 1 million, not 10 thousand.

options.label: 100 thousand
options.feedback: 100 thousand is the hundred-thousand itself — the STARTING rung here. 10 times that reaches 1 million.

widget.prompt: Match each bundle of 10 to the rung it becomes.

pairErrors.feedback: 10 hundred-thousands is one rung ABOVE a hundred-thousand — that bundle makes 1 million.

widget.missFeedback: Each bundle of 10 climbs exactly one rung: thousands → ten-thousand → hundred-thousand → million.
widget.successFeedback: 10 thousands, 10 ten-thousands, and 10 hundred-thousands each climb one rung higher.

explanationVariants: Climbing from ten-thousands to millions is two rungs (ten-thousand → hundred-thousand → million), so it takes 10 × 10 = 100 ten-thousands.
One rung up is ×10 (100 hundred-thousands... wait, one rung is 10 hundred-thousands per million); two rungs from ten-thousands is 10 × 10 = 100.

widget.prompt: How many ten-thousands are in one million?

commonErrors.feedback: 10 only climbs ONE rung (ten-thousand to hundred-thousand). Millions is two rungs up from ten-thousands: 10 × 10 = 100.
1000 climbs three rungs' worth. From ten-thousands to millions is two rungs: 10 × 10 = 100.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Count the rungs from ten-thousands to millions, then multiply 10 that many times.

hints: List every place name from ones to millions: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten-thousands, hundred-thousands, millions.
Count the GAPS between those names, not the names themselves.
explanationVariants: There are 7 place names from ones to millions, but only 6 gaps (rungs) between them — which is exactly why 1,000,000 has 6 zeros.
Ones to millions spans 6 ×10 steps, matching the 6 zeros in 1,000,000.

widget.prompt: Climbing the ladder from ones all the way to millions (ones → tens → hundreds → thousands → ten-thousands → hundred-thousands → millions), how many ×10 rungs do you climb?

commonErrors.feedback: 7 counts the seven PLACE NAMES themselves. The number of ×10 STEPS between them is one less: 6.
5 stops one rung short. Counting every gap from ones to millions gives 6 rungs.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Count the gaps between consecutive place names, not the names themselves.

steps.body: The ladder, climbed to the top.
takeaways: Every place value is 10 times the place to its right — the same rule at every rung.
Past thousands, the names continue: ten-thousand, hundred-thousand, million.
Six ×10 rungs separate ones from millions — which is why a million has six zeros.
steps.teaser: next: instantly shifting any number ten times bigger or ten times smaller.

concept.body: Quick rewind. **Every place is 10 times the place before it.** Ten ones make a ten. Ten tens make a hundred. Ten hundreds make a thousand. The pattern never changes — it just keeps climbing with new names.

explanationVariants: 10 tens bundle into 1 hundred — the ladder rule.

widget.prompt: How many tens are in one hundred?

options.feedback: 100 counts the ONES in a hundred, not the tens. A hundred is 10 tens.
1 would mean a ten and a hundred are equal — they're not. A hundred is 10 tens.
